description: Pedagogical principles used to explain teaching choices. These records describe documented frameworks or evidence-supported teaching ideas; they are not labels for countries or claims about how all teachers in a jurisdiction teach.
use_rules: Do not use a principle to describe national classroom practice unless comparative classroom evidence supports that claim.
Keep a named programme, such as NCETM teaching for mastery, separate from statutory curriculum requirements.
When a principle is recommended in MathBridge, explain the mathematical purpose and the evidence source.

principles.name_en: Link concrete, visual and symbolic representations
principles.name_cn: 连接具体、图示与符号表征
principles.description: Use objects, drawings or diagrams to make a mathematical relationship visible, then connect the same relationship explicitly to equations and symbols.
principles.why_it_matters: A representation is useful when it helps pupils see mathematical structure and transfer that structure to another representation or to symbols.
principles.evidence_scope: Teaching guidance and evidence-reviewed elementary intervention guidance.
principles.use_rule: Do not present 'concrete-pictorial-abstract' as a fixed universal sequence. Choose and connect representations according to the concept and pupil need.

principles.description: An NCETM teaching framework built around coherent sequencing, representation and structure, mathematical thinking, fluency and variation.
principles.why_it_matters: The framework links curriculum sequencing, representations, reasoning and practice rather than treating fluency and understanding as separate goals.
principles.use_rule: Label this as NCETM teaching-for-mastery guidance. Do not present it as the statutory mathematics curriculum or as the method used in every school in England.

principles.description: Change selected features of examples while keeping other features constant so pupils can notice the mathematical structure, relationship or boundary being studied.
principles.why_it_matters: Carefully chosen variation directs attention to what changes, what stays the same and which features define the concept.
principles.use_rule: Do not equate every sequence of related textbook examples with formal variation pedagogy. Attach the label only where the source explicitly supports it.

principles.description: Ask pupils to explain relationships, justify conclusions, compare methods and use mathematical language to communicate why an answer or method is valid.
principles.why_it_matters: Reasoning provides evidence of how a pupil understands the mathematics and can reveal whether a correct procedure is connected to the underlying structure.
principles.evidence_scope: Curriculum/framework expectations and official teaching/textbook guidance.
principles.use_rule: Describe the specific framework expectation being compared. Do not reduce the comparison to 'one system reasons while another memorises'.

principles.name_cn: 建立在理解基础上的熟练度
principles.description: Develop accurate and efficient recall and procedures while keeping their connection to number relationships, place value and mathematical structure explicit.
principles.why_it_matters: Automatic recall and efficient procedures reduce unnecessary processing, while conceptual connections help pupils choose, explain and adapt methods.
principles.evidence_scope: Curriculum/framework expectations and official teaching/textbook guidance.
principles.use_rule: Do not treat fluency as synonymous with speed or rote repetition. Distinguish fact recall, procedural efficiency and conceptual understanding in diagnostic and teaching recommendations.
